summary: Structured output finalization hang causing long tail latency and intermittent request timeouts
description: Issue summary: Customers using the structured JSON output mode observe a small percentage (~0.8%) of requests that never reach a terminal token for the structured finalizer. Impact: AtlasHealth AI reported repeated client-side request timeouts and 5xx retries from their production traffic; affects critical clinical summarization endpoint. Environment: prod us-east, dedicated capacity on Redwood Dedicated pool. Observed behaviour: most requests complete within expected latency (50-200ms per token), but isolated requests stall at the finalization stage for 15-60s before returning or failing with a gateway timeout. This results in increased client retries and apparent duplicate calls. No obvious increase in total token usage prior to stall.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use structured output mode with JSON schema validation enabled and function-calling disabled
2) Send a batch of long-form summarization prompts (avg 1200 tokens context) at 50rps from AtlasHealth traffic pattern
3) Observe percentile latencies; reproduce by replaying production trace provided in attachment
4) Intermittent requests hang during final suffix emission and sometimes return 504 from API gateway

investigation_notes: Initial triage: pattern occurs only for structured output runs (schema validation enabled) and primarily on models with KV-cache enabled
Hypothesis 1: finalizer path performs synchronous schema validation with retries that can block on KV cache eviction under certain batch/sequence length distributions
Hypothesis 2: a small race exists between streaming termination signal and prefix/KV cache reclaim that causes finalization coroutine to wait on a mutex held by background eviction
Checked metrics: small spike in lock_waits and finalizer_queue_depth correlating with the incidents; request error traces reference 'finalizer_waiter' stack
Replayed trace in staging: reproduced ~1/1000 of requests when adding artificial jitter to eviction job; confirms contention hypothesis
Reviewed recent changes: rollout of schema-validator v1.9 two weeks ago and a kernel scheduling tweak PR merged 2026-03-08 (related PR: serving-runtime #268)
Customer note: AtlasHealth sees user-facing timeouts primarily on peak morning traffic windows; they applied local retry backoff as temporary mitigation

resolution_notes: Short-term workaround: Instructed AtlasHealth to enable 'finalizer_async=true' flag in their route config to bypass synchronous validation; customer applied and reported immediate drop in timeouts.
Hotfix: Canary deployment (5%) of schema-validator async offload implemented in serving-runtime PR #278. No regressions observed in canary for 12h.
Planned fix: Reduce lock scope around KV cache eviction and convert schema validation to async pipeline stage. PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/278
Rollout notes: full rollout scheduled 2026-03-18 with gradual 20/50/100 percent progression and SLO rollback policy. Will monitor finalizer_queue_depth and lock_waits closely.
Follow-ups: add synthetic replay harness to catch regression, update runbook playbook with structured-output troubleshooting steps, notify customers via status page if rollout impacts latency.
Customer confirmation: AtlasHealth validated reduced timeouts after flag change and asked for planned fix ETA. Support to follow up post-rollout.
public_notes: We identified a race between structured-output finalization and KV-cache eviction that can cause rare long-tail latency. Hotfix rolled out to canary and work is planned to remove synchronous validation from the critical path.
private_notes: Consider reverting schema-validator v1.9 if canary shows anomalies. SRE to schedule extended monitoring during full rollout window. Escalate to platform lead if error rate increases above 0.5% during rollout.
